Notes to Financial Results

1. The above consolidated results of Usha Martin Limited (“the Company including ESOP Trust”) and its subsidiaries (together referred as 'the Group') and two joint ventures for the quarter and six months ended September 30, 2026 have been reviewed by the Audit Committee and approved by the Board of Directors at their respective meetings held on November 13, 2026.
2. The unaudited consolidated financial results have been prepared in accordance with the recognition and measurement principles provided in Indian Accounting Standard (Ind AS) 34 on 'Interim Financial Reporting', the provisions of the Companies Act, 2013, as applicable and guidelines issued by the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) under SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulation 2015, as amended.
3. Discontinued Operations represents Steel and Bright Bar Business (SBB Business) of the Company which was transferred to Tata Steel Long Products Limited (TSLPL) [formerly known as Tata Sponge Iron Limited] as a going concern on slump sale basis during a prior year in accordance with the terms and conditions set out in Business Transfer Agreement. An amount of Rs. 6,498 lakhs [net of discounting of Rs.948 lakhs (31st March, 2026: Rs.948 lakhs)] is receivable as at September 30, 2026, pending registration of certain parcels of land in the name of TSLPL for which perpetual lease and license agreements had been executed by the Company in favour of TSLPL. Further, during the previous year ended, the Company has recognised an expense of Rs. 1,780 lakhs towards additional expenditure incurred / to be incurred by the Company in connection with the transfer of aforesaid land parcels. The liability has been created based on management’s best estimates and in accordance with the applicable accounting standards.
4(a). "The Directorate of Enforcement (“ED”), pursuant to a Provisional Attachment Order (PAO) dated 09 August 2019, issued under the provisions of the Prevention of Money Laundering Act, 2002 (“PMLA”), provisionally attached certain parcels of Holding company’s land at Ranchi, Jharkhand, valued at approximately Rs. 19,037 lakhs. The order concerns the export and domestic sale of iron ore fines during the earlier years, which the ED alleges were in contravention of the terms of the mining lease granted to the Holding company in respect of its erstwhile iron ore mines at Ghatkuri, Jharkhand. In this regard, it is pertinent to note that The Hon'ble High Court of Jharkhand at Ranchi, vide its order dated 14 February 2012, had held that leaseholders have the right to sell the iron ore, including fines, as per the terms of the mining lease which was in place at that point in time. Further, all sale/export was made by the Holding company after payment of royalties and taxes to the State Government, and after making necessary disclosures to statutory authorities. Subsequently, the PAO was confirmed by the Hon'ble Adjudicating Authority (“AA”) under the PMLA vide order dated 10 January 2020, which was challenged by the Holding company before the PMLA Appellate Tribunal, New Delhi, resulting in a status quo order dated 31 January 2020, in favour of the Holding company in respect of the attached properties. Vide order dated 18 November 2025, the PMLA Appellate Tribunal, New Delhi, disposed of the appeal filed by the Holding company without interfering with either the PAO or the order of the AA confirming the same. Further the Tribunal confirmed that the protection granted under the earlier status quo order shall continue to the extent it relates to the possession of the attached properties by the Holding company.

The ED also filed a Complaint before the Hon'ble Special Judge PMLA Cases at Ranchi, pursuant to which summoning orders were issued to the Holding company and one of its Officers. The matter is next listed on 20 November 2026, for further proceedings. Vide order dated 21 November 2024, the Special Judge CBI cases at Ranchi, took cognizance of the charge sheet filed by the Central Bureau of Investigation (“CBI”) against the Holding company, its Managing Director (MD) and one of its other officers for alleged offences under the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988 and the Indian Penal Code, 1860. Pursuant thereto, summoning orders dated 26 November 2024, were issued to the Holding company, its MD and the said officer. The matter is next listed for hearing on 20 November 2026.

The ongoing operations of the Holding company have not been affected by the aforesaid proceedings. Supported by a legal opinion obtained, management believes that the Holding company has a strong case in its favour on merit and law. Accordingly, no adjustment to these consolidated financial results in this regard has been considered necessary by the management."
4(b). "On October 2, 2020, Central Bureau of Investigation (""CBI"") had filed a First Information Report (""FIR"") against the Holding company, its Managing Director (""MD"") and certain Other Officers under the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988 and the Indian Penal Code, 1860 before the Hon'ble Special Judge, CBI, New Delhi (CBI Court, New Delhi) for allegedly trying to influence ongoing CBI investigation pertaining to the proceedings mentioned in note 4(a) above. Vide order dated 15 September 2022, the CBI Court, New Delhi had taken cognizance of the offence based on charge sheet filed by the CBI against the Holding company, its MD and certain Other Officers. The Holding company has also received summoning orders issued by the CBI Court, New Delhi, pursuant to complaint filed by Directorate of Enforcement (""ED"") under the provisions of PMLA. The Holding company strongly refutes the aforesaid allegations. The matters at CBI Court, New Delhi is scheduled to be heard on 28 November 2026 and 4 December 2026 respectively.

The Holding company has been providing information sought by the CBI and ED in this regard and intends to continue cooperating, as required by applicable laws and relevant court orders. The Holding company and its MD are taking such legal measures as considered necessary in respect of these ongoing proceedings. Supported by a legal opinion obtained, management believes that the Holding company has a strong case in its favour on merit and law in these matters. Accordingly, no adjustment to these consolidated financial results in this regard have been considered necessary by the management."
5. On November 21, 2025, the Government of India notified provisions of the Code on Wages, 2019, the Industrial Relations Code, 2020, the Code on Social Security, 2020 and the Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code, 2020 (collectively referred to as the ‘New Labour Codes’) which consolidate twenty- nine existing labour laws into a unified framework governing employee benefits during employment and post-employment. The Company has assessed and disclosed the incremental impact of these changes on the basis of legal opinion obtained and the best information available, consistent with the guidance provided by the Institute of Chartered Accountants of India. Considering the impact arising out of an enactment of the new legislation is an event of non-recurring nature, the Holding Company has presented this incremental impact consisting of gratuity and leave liability primarily arising due to change in wage definition under “Exceptional Item” in the Statement of Profit and Loss for the quarter and year ended March 31, 2026. The Holding Company continues to monitor the finalisation of rules by the Central and State Governments and clarifications from the Government on other aspects of the New Labour Codes and will account for such developments as needed.
6. The Board of Directors of the Holding Company at its meeting held on August 12, 2024, approved the 'Usha Martin Limited Employee Stock Option Plan – 2024' ("the Plan") to be implemented by fresh issuance of fully paid-up equity shares of the Company having a face value of Rs.1 and/or secondary acquisition of equity shares through the Usha Martin Limited Employees Welfare Trust (“ESOP Trust”). The Holding Company has acquired a total of 3,41,500 shares through the ESOP Trust with the corresponding accounting being done in accordance with Ind AS 102 – Share-Based Payment. The financial results of the ESOP Trust have been included in the standalone financial results of the Holding Company in accordance with the requirements of Ind AS and the cost of such treasury shares has been presented as a deduction in Other Equity.
7. "The wholly-owned subsidiary of the Holding Company, UM Cables Limited has entered into a Business Transfer Agreement (“BTA”) on September 25, 2026 to transfer Cable Business unit by way of a sale on a going concern basis to R R Kabel Limited for a total consideration of Rs 7,700 lakhs subject to working capital adjustments as set out in the BTA. Accordingly, the related assets and liabilities of the said business are classified as ""Held for Sale"" and profit/loss from the said business are shown under 'Profit/Loss from Discontinued Operations' in the consolidated financial results. The comparative financial results has been restated accordingly.

As the transfer of the business undertaking had not been completed as at the reporting date, no profit on sale has been recognized in these consolidated financial statements. Subsequent to the reporting date, the transfer was completed with effect from the close of business on 31 October 2026 in accordance with the terms of the Business Transfer Agreement (BTA), and the resulting profit will be recognized in the period in which the transaction is completed"

Rajeev Jhawar
Managing Director
Dated : November 13, 2026
Place: Singapore
